thread:
Alex M: Quick check — I have a hypothesis: switching the int4 kernel to prefer fp8 fallback reduces p95 for short prompts but might introduce a quality cliff for long-token prompts. Can we run a focused sweep on conv-holdout-3k + summarization-set? PR #4821 touches kernel selection. Need numbers by EOD. @Maya R can you run int4->fp8 combo with seed 42?
Maya R: On it. I'll split runs into short (<128) and long (512-2048). Which model/config exactly?
Alex M: Use rwd-7b-v2, quant config `q4_int4` with fp8 fallback enabled. Example: `--model rwd-7b-v2 --quant q4_int4 --fallback fp8 --batch 8 --seq-len 512 --eval-set conv-holdout-3k --seed 42`. Keep decode default sampling for first pass.
Riley K: Heads-up: PR #4821 also changes KV-cache write/read path — could affect long-seq latency. I'll profile once Maya posts artifacts (nvprof/perf).
Maya R: Quick results (first pass): short prompts: p95=62ms (≈ -9% vs baseline), accuracy delta BLEU ≈ -0.2% absolute. Long prompts: p95=920ms (+15%), observed degenerate repeats on ~8% of samples. Uploading logs to s3.
bench-bot: Run artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-dev/bench/1829999999/maya_run.log. Summary: short_p95=62ms; long_p95=920ms; acc_delta=-0.002; degen_pct=0.08.
Jamie L: 8% degen is high. Can we rule out sampling amplification? Try deterministic decoding (temp=0) and also try a lower top_k/top_p. Also check tokenization differences between eval harness and runtime.
Priya S: I'll spin a deterministic run and also add warmup flags to rule out cold-cache effects: `--prefill-warmup=true --warmup-steps=2`.
Maya R: Deterministic run (temp=0): long degen drops to ~1.5%, long_p95 890ms, acc_delta ≈ -0.1%. So sampling amplified the degen, but the fp8 fallback path still has higher long latency and a small quality hit.
Alex M: Hmm. My working hypothesis: FP8 conversion + rounding in fallback path slightly changes logits distribution which, under sampling, increases repeat probability. Deterministic decoding reduces it. We should add a regression to Evals: 200 seeds on summarization-set and assert degen_pct < 1% for long prompts.
Riley K: Action items: (1) I'll profile kernel-level times for fp8 conversion and KV ops (nvprof + `perf record`) to pinpoint hotspots. (2) Jamie, please ask reviewer on #4821 to add a test flag `--force-fp32-kv` so we can isolate KV conversion. (3) Maya/Priya, please run the 200-seed eval + deterministic baseline and upload token diffs.
Jamie L: Will add review comments on #4821 to include the flag and a short doc note about fallback rounding. Tagging @Alex M and @Riley K — if degen_pct > 2% we should trigger a perf/regression alert.
Maya R: Starting 200-seed run now (both sampling and deterministic). ETA ~45m. Will post samples and token-level diffs when done.
bench-bot: Partial artifact: s3://redwood-dev/bench/1829999999/200seed-partial.json (30% complete).
Priya S: If profiling shows fp8 conversion is the hotspot, we can try a micro-optimization: batch fp8 conversions and fuse with KV memcpy. Low risk test: `--fp8-batch-convert=true`.
Alex M: Good. If the 200-seed confirms higher degen under sampling, my proposal: keep fp8-fallback as default for short prompts only, add canary route in Console for long prompts to stick to int4-only until we resolve. Also add a regression in CI/Evals to catch this class of quality cliffs.
Jamie L: Agreed. I'll prepare a quick rollout plan for Console (canary by seq_len) and add a short playbook for ops (how to revert to int4-only).
Maya R: Uploading completed artifacts: s3://redwood-dev/bench/1829999999/200seed-complete.tar.gz — includes token diffs and seed breakdowns. Summary: sampling degen_pct=7.8%, deterministic degen_pct=1.2%.
Riley K: I'll start kernel profiling now with the completed logs. Will share flamegraphs and a short writeup in this thread.
Alex M: Thanks everyone — this is actionable. Next sync: please drop a one-line in #eng-runtime when your task is done so I can close the ticket. :thumbsup:
Maya R: noted, will ping when CI/regression PR is up.
Jamie L: PR review started, adding tests + flag.
bench-bot: perf-alert (info): no SLA breaches, but flagging increased long-p95 for fp8-path for visibility.
